introduction:
The level-one Heisenberg current \(J(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}J_n z^{-n-1}\) obeys \([J_m,J_n]=m\delta_{m+n,0}\) and \(J_n^\dagger=J_{-n}\). Its neutral Fock vacuum satisfies \(J_n|0\rangle=0\) for \(n\ge0\). Write \(|n_1,n_2\rangle\) for the normalized state with \(n_j\) quanta of frequency \(j\) and all other modes in the vacuum. Consider the energy-two superpositions
\[
|\psi_\pm\rangle
=\frac{|2,0\rangle\pm|0,1\rangle}{\sqrt{2}}
=\frac{J_{-1}^2\pm J_{-2}}{2}|0\rangle .
\]

Tracing out either oscillator removes the cross terms, so the one-mode reduced density matrices agree. The Hermitian observable that converts one frequency-two quantum into two frequency-one quanta and back has off-diagonal matrix element \(2\), giving
\[
\mathcal O=J_{-1}^2J_2+J_{-2}J_1^2,\qquad
\langle\psi_\pm|\mathcal O|\psi_\pm\rangle=\pm2 .
\]

In the Gaussian half-space, two contractions supported in the interior combine with boundary creation modes to realize \(\mathcal O\) on polynomial states. Independently, the real harmonic scalar \(h+\bar h\) on the unit disk has \(h(z)=\sum_{n>0}Z_nz^n/n\). At a finite mode cutoff its Dirichlet action is \(S_D=\tfrac12\sum_n|Z_n|^2/n\). The ground-state amplitude is \(e^{-S_D}\). Its squared density, proportional to \(e^{-2S_D}\), gives independent complex Gaussians with \(\mathbb E|Z_n|^2=n\). Multiplication by \(2\operatorname{Re}(h'(0)^2\overline{h''(0)})\) followed by orthogonal projection onto holomorphic states gives the same operator. [The disk measurement](#ch11-relative-phase)

The operator product expansion \(J(z)J(w)\sim(z-w)^{-2}\) has a pole at collision. Let \(\Delta:X\hookrightarrow X^2\) be the diagonal of a smooth complex algebraic curve and \(j:X^2\setminus\Delta(X)\hookrightarrow X^2\) its open complement. A Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral bracket on a right \(\mathcal D_X\)-module \(L\) is a skew-symmetric \(\mathcal D_{X^2}\)-linear map satisfying Jacobi,
\[
\mu:j_*j^*(L\boxtimes L)\longrightarrow\Delta_*L .
\]
The source allows poles and the target retains normal derivatives.

For four labelled charge-one Wilson lines at level two, the outgoing charge-four highest-weight coefficient defines a rank-one local system. On the transverse slice \(\mathbb C^3\) at full collision, its perverse extensions include pairwise nonisomorphic sheaves with identical stalk and costalk ranks. The lines in the two-dimensional degree-two link cohomology form a projective line \(\mathbb P^1\). Each line is the image of the attaching map for a different extension. [The four-point collision](#ch04-gaussian-collision)

For consecutive-cut convolution \(\star\) on ordered configurations, an associative chiral algebra is an augmented \(E_1\)-algebra \(A\) with \(A_0\simeq\mathbb C\) whose bar coalgebra \(BA\) factorizes when consecutive blocks are disjoint. At arity \(n\), at most \(n\) nonempty factors contribute. This bound gives the bar–cobar equivalence \(A\simeq\Omega BA\) for such algebras. A chiral quantum group also requires a coproduct compatible with field multiplication and exchange.

Hochschild cochains \(C^\bullet(B,B)\), the derived centre of an ordinary algebra \(B\), act on its derived modules. A chiral centre would represent boundary actions compatible with collisions. Does the action of the independently defined bulk observables give an equivalence to that centre? A gravitational amplitude also requires a spatial filling whose path integral reproduces the boundary correlators under sewing, with its integration cycle and determinant line fixed. This interacting comparison remains open. [Bulk reconstruction](#bulk-action-and-centre)
